pr_title: Improve feel of fail animation for non-hitobjects
pr_body:
- Move failing logic into the Playfield and DrawableHitObject
 - Add failing animation for follow points

Closes #4956
pr_comments: I have not had a chance to properly review this yet.

I've refactored this one a bit, I moved `ArmedState.Fail` transforms into a separate function called `UpdateFailTransforms` that would be called immediately and not at a certain time (`BeginAbsoluteSequence` / `BeginDelayedSequence`).

Although this is too old, I have an idea for making the failing animation more flexible and can be applied to any drawable (like `BreakOverlay` as suggested in https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/6286#issuecomment-535759610), by introducing an `IAnimatesOnFail` interface that provides a method to be called for applying fail transforms to the drawable and will all be called from `FailAnimation` (which may be renamed to `FailAnimator` or similar), what do you think about it? @peppy @smoogipoo
That might work, but there may also be edge cases to be wary of (what happens if the state of a DHO changes after the animation is applied? does resetting (rewinding) work? etc.)
Closing this one as too old, I'll come back to this at some point.

review_comments: I don't really know much about this, is creating a bindable and binding value changed event inside the follow point the correct way to do it?
that is one way, yep. but leave this for now as this whole PR may need some more thought (was discussing with @smoogipoo yesterday and we're still undecided on direction).
i feel this is going to cause issues

I'm not sure how? it first clears all the transformations inside a follow point, and apply the following:
1. if it has failed, apply immediate fail transform from current state (clearing transformations doesn't revert values) (no delayed / absolute sequences).
2. if it hasn't, apply normal transformations at the follow point fade in time.

Reasons why?
